adds.title: Pemkot Makassar Gencarkan Pencegahan LGBT, Fokus Edukasi dan Penanganan Kasus - merdeka.com
adds.summary: Merdeka (25 April 2026, sourced from Antara) reports that the Makassar city government's women's-empowerment and child-protection agency (DP3A) is intensifying LGBT 'prevention' through socialization and education aimed at school-age children plus case handling, with counselling and a safe house for reported individuals, in response to community reports. DP3A head Ita Isdiana Anwar says most reports come from worried families, and DPRD Kota Makassar member Muchlis Misbah, citing a Komisi D monitoring meeting showing rising LGBT numbers alongside HIV/AIDS cases, backs the pending Ranperda on HIV/AIDS and LGBT as legal reinforcement. This is a dated, Makassar-city-specific record of the administrative track of the anti-LGBT push the record describes, confirming that as of April 2026 the local rule remains proposed (Ranperda) rather than enacted.

adds.title: Rancangan Perda anti-LGBT di Makassar dan Garut disebut 'tren jelang tahun politik' (Tribun News republishing BBC News Indonesia)
adds.summary: Tribun News' republication of a BBC News Indonesia report (10 January 2023, reporting by Muhammad Aidil) states that Makassar's anti-LGBT raperda had entered the 2023 local legislative programme (prolegda) as a 'priority for discussion', with two DPRD Makassar members, including PKS-faction member Azwar ST, saying the proposal models itself on Perda already passed elsewhere such as Bogor. Constitutional-law expert Bivitri Susanti calls such raperdas a 'trend ahead of the political year' that risks worsening discrimination and persecution of LGBT people, and notes the central government does little to stop discriminatory local regulations. This verifies Makassar as a recurring site of the anti-LGBT bylaw push since at least early 2023, predating the April 2025 mayoral reaffirmation the record cites, and consistent with its 'proposed, not enacted' status.

adds.title: Gender Recognition in Mexico by State | Human Rights Watch
adds.summary: HRW's state-by-state survey of Mexico records that Aguascalientes 'has not reformed its legislation to create a legal gender recognition procedure for transgender people', one of the states still lacking an administrative recognition mechanism. This directly documents the record's claim that no state-level legal gender recognition exists in Aguascalientes under the federal framework.

adds.title: Persisten terapias de conversión y violencia contra personas trans en Aguascalientes: Diversx – La Jornada Aguascalientes
adds.summary: La Jornada Aguascalientes (23 August 2026, Karla Lisseth Avalos García) reports that Diversx Laboratorio Cultural Disidente activists (Alicia Cruz, Kevin Cruz, Hened Musalem) say conversion-therapy operations still run in Aguascalientes under the guise of addiction-treatment annexes despite the legal prohibition, and that a person who escaped one of these spaces arrived at the group last year. They state trans women continue to suffer prejudice-motivated aggression, and cite the ENDISEG survey showing 7.3% of the state's population aged 15+ self-identifies as LGBTI+, the fifth-highest proportion among Mexican states. This is the first state-specific documentation for this record of ongoing anti-trans violence and family rejection in Aguascalientes beyond the absence of a recognition law.

adds.title: Suprema Corte facilita el cambio del género en actas de nacimiento en Aguascalientes - Infobae
adds.summary: Infobae (9 April 2026, Joshua Espinosa) reports that Mexico's Supreme Court, in Amparo en Revisión 430/2025 with a project by Minister Giovanni Figueroa Mejía, ruled that Aguascalientes' Civil Code requirements for gender change of birth certificates - judicial or ministerial intervention, civil trials, probative proof of identity and marginal annotations - are discriminatory and violate privacy, ordering the state's Civil Registry to grant recognition through a simple, confidential administrative procedure honoring self-perception, with a new birth certificate issued and no marginal notes revealing a prior gender. The ruling's immediate effect is limited to persons represented by the civil association that filed the amparo. This is a dated, state-specific legal development that changes the record's 'no state-level recognition' picture by adding a court-ordered administrative route in Aguascalientes.

adds.title: Gender Recognition in Mexico by State | Human Rights Watch
adds.summary: HRW's state-by-state survey records that Baja California's congress enacted a 2022 reform to the Civil Code creating an administrative procedure for legal gender recognition for adults; in June 2023 Mexico's Supreme Court struck down the law's adults-only requirement because it did not recognize the rights of transgender children and adolescents; and in 2024 the state congress passed a new reform establishing a procedure for individuals under 18 and expanding legal gender recognition to non-binary people. This is the authoritative confirmation of the exact legal-recognition timeline the record states for Baja California.

adds.title: Por muerte de Ángela, capturan a feminicida serial - Semanario ZETA
adds.summary: Zeta Tijuana (8 July 2023, Rosario Mosso Castro) reports that Brayan Rivera was presented on 6 July 2023 before US Judge Karen L. Stevenson in provisional detention for extradition, accused by Mexico of the feminicide of Ángela Carolina Acosta, killed on 24 January 2022 in room 404 of Hotel Cascadas beside Bar Hong Kong in Tijuana's tolerance zone; probable cause was determined on 29 June 2023 by the US federal court, and he was arrested at his parents' Downey, California home, where officers found the Hotel Cascadas rent receipt and rope and gloves. At a 7 July 2023 press conference the Baja California attorney general called the 30-year-old a serial perpetrator, said extradition could take from 15 days to two years, and that nearly a decade of open case files were being reviewed; the investigation had linked him to at least three feminicides - Ángela (January 2022), Elizabeth (14 February), and Karen, 28 (30 August 2021, Motel Hacienda Soler). This is the dated, local-press verification of the serial-killer counterweight in the record's Tijuana risk picture.

adds.title: Mujeres y las estadísticas negativas en BC - Semanario ZETA
adds.summary: Zeta Tijuana (8 March 2025, Rosario Mosso Castro) reports that under Baja California Governor Marina del Pilar Ávila, 1,179 women have been killed in the state while only 110 cases were typified as feminicide - a small share that underscores under-classification of lethal violence against women - and that female economic participation in the state stood at roughly 46-47%, 14th of 32 states. This state-level data supports the record's 'under-counted lethal risk' characterization for Baja California, complementing the Tijuana-specific serial-killer case.
